questions.question: Use exact complex amplitudes and column vectors. For finite sets C, S, X and a family p assigning a bijection p_s:X→X to every s∈S, the basis is A=C×(S×X). The controlled map is F_p(c,(s,x))=(c,(s,p_s(x))). The SELECT matrix is U_p(r,k)=1 if r=F_p(k), and 0 otherwise. Thus coefficient c and selector s are preserved, and no ancilla is added. All statements are exact equalities of matrices over ℂ; finite sets may be empty unless a concrete set is specified. Put D=X×(C×S), and let J(c,(s,x))=(x,(c,s)). Define U'_p(r,k)=U_p(J⁻¹(r),J⁻¹(k)). Proposition: for every C,S,X,p and every r,k∈D, U'_p(r,k)=1 exactly when r=(p_{k.2.2}(k.1),(k.2.1,k.2.2)), and it is 0 otherwise. Decide whether the stated proposition is valid under exactly the supplied assumptions. Give a mathematical reason. If it is invalid, give an exact finite basis witness and state a repair; distinguish the original proposition from the repair.
